_comment: The pinned corpus, named by its bytes rather than only by its version.
`DATASET_VERSION` in scripts/lib/paths.py said 6.1, which meant whatever
Harvard served as 6.1 that day; scripts/00_fetch_data.py then had to ask the
API what those bytes should be before it could check the ones on disk. That
made a network call the precondition for verifying a corpus already present,
and in August 2026 an AWS WAF challenge in front of the archive turned that
into a hard stop for every deploy - see the comment block in 00.
A published Dataverse version is immutable, so these checksums are constants.
Recording them makes the pin complete: the pipeline can now prove the corpus
is the pinned one with no network at all, and a download - when one is
actually needed - is still checked against Harvard's own MD5s.
Provenance: read from the dataset version record at the URL below on
13 August 2026 and confirmed byte-for-byte against the local corpus. Every
value here is Harvard's, not computed from a local file. Re-read them with
Changing the pin means changing `version` here and DATASET_VERSION together;
00 refuses to run if the two disagree. This file is under config/, so the
deploy workflow's derived cache key already covers it.
